questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The size of Jupiter and Mars is similar.
The density of Saturn is similar to that of Earth.
The size of Earth and Venus is almost similar.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option** **4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth and Venus are often referred to as "sister planets" due to their similar sizes, with Earth having a diameter of about 12,742 km and Venus around 12,104 km.
 
• Mars is not the warmest planet; Venus is the hottest due to its thick atmosphere that traps heat.
 
• Saturn has a much lower density than Earth. Saturn is the least dense planet in the solar system, with a density less than that of water.
 
• Jupiter is significantly larger than Mars; in fact, it is the largest planet in our solar system, while Mars is much smaller.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter's diameter** is about 139,822 km, making it more than **6 **times larger than Earth.
 
• **Mars **has a **thin atmosphere** and average temperatures around -80 degrees Fahrenheit (-62 degrees Celsius), much colder than Earth.
 
• **Venus **has a dense atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, contributing to its **extreme greenhouse effect** and surface temperatures around 900 degrees Fahrenheit (475 degrees Celsius).
 
• **Saturn **is famous for its prominent** ring system**, which is made up of ice and rock particles ranging in size.
 
• While Earth is a rocky planet, both Venus and Mars are also terrestrial, but they differ significantly in terms of surface conditions and atmospheres.
 
• Earth has a stronger **gravitational pull** compared to Mars and Venus due to its larger mass, affecting the potential for retaining an atmosphere and sustaining life.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7243bfe5bb325520505188e575f0b801e8f6c29efc8aeb7fd65e10c4b336088.png]

questions.question: In 1835, who developed the process of applying a thin layer of metallic silver to one side of a clear glass pane and created the first mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justus von Liebig**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Justus von Liebig (1803-1873) was a **German chemist** and is often referred to as the **father of modern organic chemistry**.
 
• In 1835, Justus von Liebig developed a process to coat glass with metallic silver, resulting in the creation of the **first modern mirror.**
 
• Liebig's work in agriculture led to the **development of fertilizers**, which improved crop yields and agricultural practices.
 
• Liebig received various honors for his contributions to science, including being elected as a** member of several prestigious scientific societies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C.V. Raman:**

 
 
• An Indian physicist known for his discovery of the **Raman Effect** in 1928, which explained the scattering of light and led to advancements in spectroscopy.
 
• He received the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1930** for his work.
 
 
 
• **Victor Francis Hess:**
 
 
• An Austrian physicist recognized for discovering **cosmic rays** in **1912**, which contributed significantly to the field of high-energy physics.
 
• He won the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1936** for his contributions to the study of cosmic radiation.
 
 
 
• **C.H. Townes:**
 
 
• An American physicist known for co-developing the laser and maser technologies, which have numerous applications in communication and medicine.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1964** for his fundamental work in the field of **quantum** **electronics**.

questions.question: In MS Word, which option allows you to quickly remove all formatting from selected text while retaining the underlying text content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clear Formatting**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "**Clear Formatting" **option allows you to **quickly remove all applied formatting** (like bold, italics, font size, color, etc.) from the selected text while preserving the actual text content.
 
• It can be found under the Home tab in the Font group, represented by an eraser icon labeled "Clear Formatting."
 
• You can also use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Spacebar** to clear character formatting or **Ctrl + Q** to clear paragraph formatting.
 
• This feature is useful when you want to revert text to the default formatting without manually changing individual formatting elements.
 
• It removes custom formatting but retains the document's underlying style settings, such as the default **font and paragraph styles set for the document.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cut function in MS Word**

 
 
• The Cut function removes the selected text or object from its original location and places it in the clipboard, allowing you to paste it elsewhere in the document.
 
• You can quickly perform the Cut action using the keyboard shortcut** Ctrl + X**.
 
• The Cut option is typically used when you want to relocate content within the document or transfer it between documents.
 
 
 
• **Paste Special in MS Word**
 
 
• The Paste Special feature allows you to paste copied content in various formats, such as plain text, formatted text, or an image, depending on how you want the content to appear.
 
• You can access Paste Special by using the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Alt + V **or by selecting it from the Paste drop-down in the Home tab.
 
• It is useful when you need to control how content is pasted, for example, when you want to paste data as unformatted text or as a specific object, such as a picture or **HTML content.**
 
 
 
• **Format Painter in MS Word**
 
 
• Format Painter is a tool that allows you to copy formatting (such as font, color, size, and style) from one section of text and apply it to another, making formatting consistent across the document.
 
• It is located in the Home tab under the **Clipboard group,** represented by a **paintbrush icon.**
 
• You can use Format Painter by selecting the text with the desired formatting, clicking the **Format Painter icon**, and then selecting the text you want to apply the formatting to. **Double-clicking the icon** allows you to apply formatting to multiple sections.

questions.question: The Salal Project, also called the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is on which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenab.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Salal Project, also known as the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is located on the **Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir, **India.
 
• The Chenab River originates in the Himalayas and flows approximately** 960 km through India and Pakistan**, and is one of the five rivers of Punjab, crucial for irrigation and agriculture.
 
• The project has a total installed capacity of** 690 MW,** generating electricity to meet regional demand.
 
• The Chenab also has major tributaries, including the **Jhelum and Ravi rivers,** contributing to its significance.
 
• The Salal Project plays a vital role in flood control and irrigation in addition to power generation, and it is managed by the **National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4b9e6b0700bcf754488b69efa41a79c2ad91fed704ecfb382a9d71f2577646b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ravi:
 
 
• The Ravi River flows approximately **720 km** and is another important river in the region, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• It is** one of the five rivers of Punjab, and the Ranjit Sagar Dam **built on this river provides hydroelectric power and irrigation.
 
 
 
• Ganga:
 
 
• The Ganga River **originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand** and flows for about **2,525 km** through northern India into Bangladesh.
 
• Considered sacred in Hinduism, the Ganga is vital for millions who depend on it for water and agriculture, and efforts like the** Ganga Action Plan** aim to address pollution and conserve the river.
 
 
 
• Krishna:
 
 
• The Krishna River originates in the **Western Ghats of Maharashtra **and flows approximately 1,400 km through Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This river is crucial for irrigation and drinking water supply, with major projects like the **Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam dams **supporting its significance.

questions.question: Suppose a mine worker asks his son, aged 9 years, to help him in his work instead of going to school. Which Article of the Constitution of India will be violated in this case?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 24 of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in hazardous industries, including mines.
 
• In this scenario, asking a 9-year-old child to help in the mine instead of attending school would violate this provision aimed at protecting children from exploitation.
 
• The article reflects the commitment to children's rights and their right to education, ensuring that they are not subjected to harmful working conditions.
 
• The Constitution emphasizes the importance of education for children, aligning with various laws, such as the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act.
 
• Violating Article 24 undermines efforts to eradicate child labor and promote the well-being of children in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 20:
 
 
• Article 20 provides **protection against retroactive criminal legislation** and ensures that no person is convicted of an offense except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission.
 
 
 
• Article 18:
 
 
• Article 18 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth

__
 
• The Kailasa Temple, built by the** Rashtrakutas**, is located in Ellora, Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is one of the most remarkable rock-cut temples in the world and is **dedicated to Lord Shiva.**
 
• The temple complex, which includes 34 monasteries and temples, is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The Kailasa Temple, **also known as Kailasanatha Temple**, is famous for its **monolithic structure**, carved from a single rock.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Hampi was the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** from the 14th to the 16th century.
 
• The site is famous for its **Dravidian architecture** and includes over 1,600 ancient monuments, temples, and structures.
 
• **Kanchipuram (Kanchi)**, is a city in Tamil Nadu, India, known for its rich history, cultural significance, and beautiful temples.
 
• It served as a capital for various South Indian dynasties, including the **Pallavas, Cholas, and Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• The **Amravati Stupa** is one of the largest stupas in India and is renowned for its intricately carved stone.
 
• Amravati has been designated as the new capital city of the state of Andhra Pradesh, **established after the bifurcation of the state in 2014.**

questions.question: Folk music sung on the birth of a child in some Indian states like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, etc. is called _____.

__
 
• Folk music sung on the birth of a child in some Indian states like** Bihar, Uttar Pradesh**, and others is called **"Suhag" or "Suhag geet."**

• These songs are often** sung by female relatives**, including grandmothers, aunts, and sisters.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes application software?

options.text: Application software is designed to perform specific tasks or functions to meet the user’s needs.
Application software is used only by software developers and does not impact regular users.
Application software is responsible for managing and controlling computer hardware components.
Application software refers to the operating system that provides a user-friendly interface to interact with the computer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Application software is designed to perform specific tasks or functions to meet the user’s needs.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Application software** refers to programs designed to help users **perform specific tasks, enhancing efficiency and productivity.**
 
• These user-centric programs include examples like Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe Photoshop, and web browsers such as Google Chrome.</li&

questions.question: The velocity of circulation of money will be higher when the ________ is less than the requirements of the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**demand for money.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The demand for money refers to the **desired holding of financial assets in the form of money** (cash or bank deposits) rather than investments.
 
• The demand for money is influenced by several factors.
 
• People need money for daily transactions **(transaction motive)** and to cover unforeseen expenses **(precautionary motive)**.
 
• Additionally, money is held for future investment opportunities** (speculative motive)**.
 
• The demand for money is also** inversely related to interest rates**; higher interest rates reduce the demand for holding money, while lower rates increase it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Supply of money** refers to the** total amount of monetary assets** available in an economy at a specific time. An increase in the money supply can lead to inflation if not matched by economic growth.
 
• **Elasticity of money** is not a standard economic term but could refer to how responsive the demand for money is to changes in interest rates or other economic variables.
 
• **The velocity of money** is a key indicator used alongside GDP to gauge the economic health and activity level.

questions.question: ‘The Life Divine’, ‘The Synthesis of Yoga’ and ‘Savitri’ are the popular works of which of the following extremist freedom fighters of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aurobindo Ghosh was an **Indian philosopher**, yogi, guru, poet, and nationalist.
 
• He was one of the influential leaders in the early part of the Indian independence movement.
 
• His notable works include '**The Life Divine**', '**The Synthesis of Yoga**', and '**Savitri**'.
 
• He later moved to Pondicherry and founded the Aurobindo Ashram, dedicating his life to spiritual practice and writing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extremist Freedom Fighters:**

 
 
• Extremist freedom fighters believed in more radical approaches to achieve independence from British rule.
 
• They often advocated for direct action, including protests, boycotts, and sometimes even armed struggle.
 
• Prominent extremist leaders included **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**, collectively known as the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghosh's Contribution to Indian Freedom Movement:**
 
 
• Aurobindo was initially involved in the Indian freedom struggle and was a member of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was associated with the revolutionary activities and was arrested in the **Alipore Bomb Case in 1908**, though later acquitted.
 
• After his acquittal, Aurobindo gradually retreated from active politics and focused on spiritual and philosophical pursuits.
 
 
 
• **The Life Divine:**
 
 
• This is a book written by Aurobindo Ghosh that expounds on his philosophical ideas and spiritual experiences.
 
• It addresses the nature of reality, the evolution of consciousness, and the ultimate goal of human life.
 
 
 
• **The Synthesis of Yoga:**
 
 
• Another significant work by Aurobindo, it elaborates on the integration of various paths of yoga (such as** Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, and Jnana Yoga**) into a comprehensive spiritual practice.
 
 
 
• **Savitri:**
 
 
• An epic **poem **written by Aurobindo, it is considered one of his masterpieces and is based on the **legend of Savitri and Satyavan **from the **Mahabharata**.
 
• The poem explores themes of **human destiny, love, and transformation**.

questions.question: What is the literacy rate of males in India as per the report published in the National Survey of India-2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.847**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** literacy rate of males **in India, as per the **National Survey of India-2022**, is **0.847**.
 
• This figure represents the percentage of male individuals aged 7 and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• The literacy rate is a crucial indicator of a country's educational development and is used for various policy and planning purposes.
 
• India has seen a significant increase in literacy rates over the decades due to various government initiatives and educational reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• It is a key indicator of **educational attainment **in a country.
 
• Higher literacy rates are associated with better socio-economic conditions and enhanced quality of life.
 
 
 
• **National Survey of India**
 
 
• The National Survey of India conducts various surveys to gather data on different socio-economic parameters, including literacy rates.
 
• These surveys help in formulating policies and programs aimed at improving the country's overall development.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Improve Literacy**
 
 
• **Saakshar Bharat Mission:** Launched in **2009**, it aims to further promote and strengthen adult education, especially among women.
 
• **Right to Education Act (RTE):** Enacted in **2009**, it mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14.
 
• **National Literacy Mission:** Launched in **1988**, it aims to achieve a sustainable threshold level of 75% literacy by focusing on women and other disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Achieving Higher Literacy Rates**
 
 
• **Regional Disparities:** Significant variations in literacy rates exist between different regions and states in India.
 
• **Gender Inequality:** Despite improvements, female literacy rates lag behind male literacy rates.
 
• **Dropout Rates:** High dropout rates, especially in rural areas, hinder the overall improvement in literacy rates.
 
• **Quality of Education:** Ensuring quality education and reducing the student-teacher ratio remains a challenge.
